# Timer (`timer`)

Named countdowns, several at once: time left, pause, add a minute, cancel, and a finished alert.

Group: Home controls. Styles: `import '@mosaic-home/design-system/css/home';` (or `style.css`).

## Web API

`createTimer` (types in `dist/web/home/media-voice/timer.d.ts`): `.mh-timer`: named countdowns, several at once, as a labelled group with a `__list` of `__item`s (`.is-running | is-paused | is-finished`). Each item has a `__dial` (an SVG `__ring` drained by `--_left`, and a `__glyph`), `__text` (`__name`, the `__time` with `role="timer"`, the `__state` word) and `__actions` (pause or resume, add a minute, cancel; a finished one offers add and `__stop`). Running timers are drawn from their end time and re-checked once a second and when the page wakes, so a sleeping tab is right again at once. A hidden polite live region says when a timer starts, pauses, resumes or finishes; the seconds themselves aren't spoken.

```ts
export function createTimer(options: TimerOptions): TimerHandle;

export interface TimerOptions extends TimerData, TimerEvents {}

export interface TimerHandle {
  el: HTMLDivElement;
  update(options: TimerOptions): void;
  /** Stops the ticking and the wake-up listener. */
  destroy(): void;
}

export interface TimerData {
  timers: readonly TimerItem[];
  /** Accessible name of the group (default "Timers"). */
  label?: string;
  /** Seconds the add button adds (default 60). */
  addStep?: number;
  labels?: Partial<TimerLabels>;
  /** The clock, in ms since the epoch (default `Date.now`); for tests and synced clocks. */
  now?: () => number;
}

export interface TimerEvents {
  onPause?: (id: string) => void;
  onResume?: (id: string) => void;
  /** The add button: `seconds` is `addStep`. Also offered on a finished timer, to run it a little longer. */
  onAdd?: (id: string, seconds: number) => void;
  onCancel?: (id: string) => void;
  /** Silences a finished timer (default `onCancel`). */
  onStop?: (id: string) => void;
  /** A running timer reached zero on this screen (once per timer), before the data says so. */
  onFinish?: (id: string) => void;
}

/** One countdown. Running timers carry their end time, so the time left is right even after the page slept. */
export interface TimerItem {
  id: string;
  /** "Pasta", "Tea"; without one the timer is called by `labels.timer`. */
  name?: string | null;
  /** The length it was set to, in seconds: draws the ring. */
  duration: number;
  state: TimerState;
  /** Running: when it ends, in ms since the epoch (`Date.now()` clock). */
  endsAt?: number | null;
  /** Paused (or running without `endsAt`): seconds left. */
  remaining?: number | null;
}

/** Every word the timers show or speak. `{name}` is the timer's name, `{time}` a time like "1:00". */
export interface TimerLabels {
  group: string;
  empty: string;
  /** Name of a timer that has none. */
  timer: string;
  running: string;
  paused: string;
  finished: string;
  pause: string;
  resume: string;
  /** Visible text of the add button. */
  addText: string;
  add: string;
  cancel: string;
  /** Visible text of the button that silences a finished timer. */
  stopText: string;
  stop: string;
  /** Spoken when a timer appears, pauses, resumes or finishes. */
  started: string;
  pausedNotice: string;
  resumedNotice: string;
  finishedNotice: string;
}
```

## Web example

```ts
import { createTimer, type TimerEvents, type TimerItem } from '@mosaic-home/design-system/web';

let timers: TimerItem[] = [
  { id: 'pasta', name: 'Pasta', duration: 600, state: 'running', endsAt: Date.now() + 431_000 },
  { id: 'bread', name: 'Bread proving', duration: 5400, state: 'paused', remaining: 3725 },
];

/** Seconds left on a timer. */
const left = (t: TimerItem): number =>
  t.state === 'running' && t.endsAt ? Math.max(0, (t.endsAt - Date.now()) / 1000) : (t.remaining ?? 0);

// Returning null removes the timer.
const change = (id: string, next: (t: TimerItem) => TimerItem | null): void => {
  timers = timers.flatMap((t) => (t.id === id ? (next(t) ?? []) : [t]));
  timer.update({ timers, ...events });
};

const events: TimerEvents = {
  onPause: (id) => change(id, (t) => ({ ...t, state: 'paused', remaining: left(t), endsAt: null })),
  onResume: (id) =>
    change(id, (t) => ({ ...t, state: 'running', endsAt: Date.now() + left(t) * 1000, remaining: null })),
  onAdd: (id, seconds) =>
    change(id, (t) => {
      const rest = left(t) + seconds;
      const duration = Math.max(t.duration, rest);
      return t.state === 'paused'
        ? { ...t, remaining: rest, duration }
        : { ...t, state: 'running', endsAt: Date.now() + rest * 1000, remaining: null, duration };
    }),
  onFinish: (id) => change(id, (t) => ({ ...t, state: 'finished', endsAt: null })),
  onCancel: (id) => change(id, () => null),
  onStop: (id) => change(id, () => null),
};

const timer = createTimer({ timers, ...events });

document.body.append(timer.el);
```

## React example

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Timer } from '@mosaic-home/design-system/react';
import type { TimerItem } from '@mosaic-home/design-system/web';

/** Seconds left on a timer. */
const left = (t: TimerItem): number =>
  t.state === 'running' && t.endsAt ? Math.max(0, (t.endsAt - Date.now()) / 1000) : (t.remaining ?? 0);

export function TimerExample() {
  const [timers, setTimers] = useState<TimerItem[]>(() => [
    { id: 'pasta', name: 'Pasta', duration: 600, state: 'running', endsAt: Date.now() + 431_000 },
    { id: 'bread', name: 'Bread proving', duration: 5400, state: 'paused', remaining: 3725 },
  ]);
  // Returning null removes the timer.
  const change = (id: string, next: (t: TimerItem) => TimerItem | null) =>
    setTimers((list) => list.flatMap((t) => (t.id === id ? (next(t) ?? []) : [t])));
  const remove = (id: string) => change(id, () => null);
  const resume = (id: string) =>
    change(id, (t) => ({ ...t, state: 'running', endsAt: Date.now() + left(t) * 1000, remaining: null }));
  const add = (id: string, seconds: number) =>
    change(id, (t) => {
      const rest = left(t) + seconds;
      const duration = Math.max(t.duration, rest);
      return t.state === 'paused'
        ? { ...t, remaining: rest, duration }
        : { ...t, state: 'running', endsAt: Date.now() + rest * 1000, remaining: null, duration };
    });
  return (
    <Timer
      timers={timers}
      onPause={(id) => change(id, (t) => ({ ...t, state: 'paused', remaining: left(t), endsAt: null }))}
      onResume={resume}
      onAdd={add}
      onFinish={(id) => change(id, (t) => ({ ...t, state: 'finished', endsAt: null }))}
      onCancel={remove}
      onStop={remove}
    />
  );
}
```
